name: basement-worms-eye
idea: An extreme low angle from floor level in a windowless council records basement, ultra-wide lens, looking up past the gang to a paper stack that climbs out of frame into flickering cold fluorescent tubes. Five gang members in muted modern workwear (hoodies, puffer jackets, hi-vis) and dark masks in different colours stand at its foot with their heads tipped back. Only their mask rings and red triangles catch the light. The palette is green-white fluorescent and grey steel shelving, and the top sheet of the stack, seen edge-on, reads THE RULES. Focus is deep throughout so the stack feels endless.

name: parr-flash-council-office
idea: Midday in a beige modern British council office reception (laminate counter, ticket dispenser, faded leaflets, plastic chairs), shot head-on in a Martin Parr manner with direct on-camera flash and a wide lens, so every colour comes out saturated and slightly cheap. The gang wear bright, clashing balaclavas, one each in lime, pink, orange, cobalt and yellow, with tracksuits and cheap anoraks, and they queue as if waiting to be seen. A paper stack fills the space behind the counter and rises through a broken ceiling tile, with a laminated A4 sign taped to it reading THE RULES. The camera sits at medium distance, the frame is crowded with detail, and the joke is deadpan.

name: crewdson-terrace-blue-hour
idea: A wide, staged tableau at blue hour on an ordinary British terraced street: wheelie bins, parked hatchbacks, lit front windows. A colossal paper stack stands in the middle of the road as tall as the houses. The gang are small figures in the lower third, standing in a loose line in modern streetwear and looking up at it. In the Gregory Crewdson manner, every practical light is lit on purpose: streetlamps, window glow, and one hard white light raking up the face of the stack, where THE RULES is printed on the top sheet's edge. The sky is deep cobalt, the rest is warm sodium, and the mood is quiet and uncanny, with the stack in sharp focus.

name: profile-close-window-light
idea: A tight close-up of one gang member seen three-quarter from their left side so the red triangle over the left eye is clearly visible, head tilted back to look up, shot on an 85mm lens at f/1.8. Late-afternoon golden window light falls across a charcoal knitted mask with the white ring stitched round it, and a gloved hand rests on the collar of a modern waxed jacket. Behind them, soft and out of focus, a wall of stacked paper fills the upper frame, with just enough of one sheet legible to read THE RULES. The palette is warm amber against cool paper white. The picture is about the mask's texture and the scale implied by looking up.

name: overhead-from-the-top
idea: The camera sits on top of the stack at night and looks straight down its sheer paper cliff to the gang far below on a wet concrete floor, foreshortened, their faces turned up towards the lens. The top sheet in the near foreground reads THE RULES in bold black type, crisp and in focus, while the gang are small and slightly soft. The only light comes from torch beams the gang point upwards, plus a faint sodium spill from a high warehouse window, so the scene is mostly black with pools of white. Each mask is a different dark colour, and the ring and red triangle glint in the torchlight. Vertigo in reverse: we are the rules looking down at them.

name: high-key-white-monolith
idea: A vast empty white space, with seamless floor and walls, flat shadowless high-key light, and the atmosphere of a minimalist gallery. The paper stack stands dead centre as a clean rectangular monolith, like a Taryn Simon sculpture, with THE RULES printed neatly in small black type on a label at its base. The gang stand in a neat row in front of it with their backs half turned, looking up, in bright Pussy Riot-style knitted balaclavas of different saturated colours and plain modern clothes in black and grey. The camera is far back, symmetrical and still. The only colour in a white world is the masks and their red triangles.
